proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current experiment class permits response means of order \(n^{-1}\) and collapsing response variance.  The added theorem then gives schedule-independent undercoverage, even though both bounded-Lipschitz approximations are valid, so an affirmative answer to the old question would not identify rare-margin face switching or a sharp \(n\kappa_n^3\) threshold.  The proposed question honestly narrows the intended inquiry to a subclass of \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\) satisfying a yet-to-be-characterized primitive nondegeneracy condition; it does not assume coverage.

proposed_core_edits.name: \mathbb P^0
proposed_core_edits.reason: The directive requires a named, schedule-independent triangular-array experiment carrying the response-boundary counterexample.

proposed_core_edits.name: \mathfrak Q_{\kappa}
proposed_core_edits.reason: The directive requires the singleton experiment class over which the two uniform approximation suprema reduce to verified single-array discrepancies.
This construction names the all-zero-event array, its ridge estimator and multiplier, and the mandated singleton class without asserting any of their load-bearing properties.
The narrowed OEQ must explicitly depend on the response-boundary theorem that exposes the missing prerequisite; all other formal dependencies are preserved.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Characterize a minimal primitive uniform response-nondegeneracy or anti-concentration condition that excludes the response-boundary array without assuming coverage, and then determine whether bounded \(n\kappa_n^3\) forces schedule-quantified undercoverage through rare-margin optimal-face switching on that repaired subclass.
open_obligations.obstruction: The frozen bounded-Lipschitz Gaussian and multiplier approximations control absolute weak distance but impose no response-interiority, variance lower bound, relative variance consistency, or quantile anti-concentration.  They therefore allow a degenerate Gaussian limit and an atom at the limiting critical value, for which vanishing-width intervals miss an \(n^{-1}\)-scale ridge discrepancy with nonvanishing probability.
open_obligations.attempted: The two-context all-zero-event construction was evaluated for every positive numerical-delta schedule.  It proves genuine critical-value and coverage distortion, but that distortion persists independently of rare margins and so cannot certify procedural sharpness of the \(n\kappa_n^3\) boundary.  Reusing it as a rare-margin witness would misattribute the mechanism.
